tomato|early blight.what_it_is: A fungal leaf disease that makes dark spots with rings on leaves and fruit.
what_to_do: Remove and destroy infected plant parts and crop debris from the field.
Avoid wetting the leaves when you water; use furrow or drip irrigation if possible.
prevention: Rotate tomato with crops that are not hosts of this disease.
Stake the plants so air can move between them.
Use healthy, disease-free seed and transplants.
sources: TNAU Agritech Portal, Tomato Early Blight: https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_protection/tomato_diseases_2.html

Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station, Early Blight of Tomato fact sheet: https://portal.ct.gov/-/media/caes/documents/publications/fact_sheets/plant_pathology_and_ecology/earlyblightoftomato032912pdf.pdf

tomato|late blight.what_it_is: A fast-spreading disease that makes dark, oily-looking patches on leaves and stems and can destroy the whole crop.
what_to_do: Remove and destroy infected plants as soon as you see the disease.
Remove leftover tomato and potato plants, cull piles and plant debris from the field.
Avoid overhead or sprinkler irrigation if you can.
Do not use too much nitrogen fertiliser.
prevention: Plant only healthy transplants that are free of late blight.
Do not grow tomato or potato in the same field for two years.
Ask your Krishi Vigyan Kendra about resistant varieties for your area.
sources: Utah State University Extension, Late Blight: https://extension.usu.edu/planthealth/ipm/notes_ag/veg-late-blight.php
UC IPM, Tomato Pest Management Guidelines: https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/r783100211.html
UConn, Late Blight of Tomato and Potato: https://homegarden.cahnr.uconn.edu/factsheets/late-blight-of-tomato-and-potato

potato|late blight.what_it_is: A fast-spreading disease that makes dark, greasy-looking patches on leaves and stems and can destroy the whole crop.
what_to_do: Remove and destroy infected plants as soon as you see the disease.
Remove cull piles, plant debris and leftover potato and tomato plants from the field.
Avoid overhead or sprinkler irrigation if you can.
Do not use too much nitrogen fertiliser.
prevention: Do not grow potato or tomato in the same field for two years.
Ask your Krishi Vigyan Kendra about resistant varieties for your area.
sources: Utah State University Extension, Late Blight: https://extension.usu.edu/planthealth/ipm/notes_ag/veg-late-blight.php
UConn, Late Blight of Tomato and Potato: https://homegarden.cahnr.uconn.edu/factsheets/late-blight-of-tomato-and-potato

corn|common rust.what_it_is: A fungal disease that makes small, rust-coloured to dark brown pustules on both sides of the leaves.
what_to_do: Plant resistant maize hybrids in the next planting.
Ask your Krishi Vigyan Kendra which resistant hybrids suit your area.
prevention: Choose resistant maize hybrids when you buy seed.
sources: University of Minnesota Extension, Common rust on corn: https://extension.umn.edu/corn-pest-management/common-rust-corn
Dey et al. 2017, Screening of maize inbred lines and hybrids against common rust, UAS Dharwad: https://www.ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/view/1151
